facts: 12.0 pts, 12.8 after the slate's own level
Pittsburgh -12.9, which is 9.4 past the market
Pittsburgh +14.6 (18th) vs North Carolina +1.8 (tied 64th), home edge +2.7
5-0, 4-1 ATS, 38.4 points a game and 13.4 allowed
7th Success Rate, 14th Finishing Drives, 93.1 run defense
2-2, 24.0 for and 19.5 against, offense 120th in Explosiveness
paras: Book has Pittsburgh -3.5. The rating says -15.5 and the points check, built only from each team's own 2026 point differential plus home field, says -12.9. Two measures sharing no inputs land nine and twelve points past a field goal.

Pittsburgh are 5-0 and the margin is not an accident. They score 38.4 and allow 13.4, the defense ranks 7th in Success Rate and 14th in Finishing Drives on a 90.2 defensive grade and 93.1 against the run, and the offense grades 84.5 passing behind an 82.8 pass block grade.

North Carolina are 2-2 at 24.0 points a game. The offense ranks 49th in Success Rate but 120th in Explosiveness, so it moves the ball without threatening, and that is the profile a defense ranked 131st in Explosiveness allowed is built to live with. Their own defense ranks 106th in Success Rate.

The risk is the price being short for a reason the numbers cannot see. Three and a half points on a 5-0 team against a .500 opponent is the market saying it does not believe the gap, and a 12-point disagreement with two independent measures usually means someone knows something. Pittsburgh's 59.4 tackling grade is the one soft number to point at.

facts: 6.0 pts, 6.8 after the slate's own level

paras: Book has Ole Miss -9.5 on the road. The rating still makes Vanderbilt a 3.5-point underdog, so it is not calling an upset, but the points check has the game at a pick'em. Both reads put the fair number well inside a touchdown.

Ole Miss are the better team and also the leakier one. They score 35.5 but concede 30.8, and the defense ranks 127th in Success Rate and 109th in Finishing Drives on a 50.5 coverage grade and a 44.7 tackling grade. A team that gives up 30 a game laying nine and a half on the road is the whole position.

Vanderbilt are ordinary on offense, 104th in Success Rate and 116th in Finishing Drives behind a 50.9 pass block grade, which is why this is taking points rather than backing a winner. What they do have is a defense ranked 69th with an 82.3 coverage grade against a passing offense that grades 86.2.

The pace argument cuts against. Ole Miss play the 6th-fastest tempo in the country against Vanderbilt's 110th, so there are more possessions than a home underdog wants. Ole Miss being 1-3 against the spread is the counterweight: the market has already been asking too much of them.

Northern Illinois's 82.0 tackling grade is their one competent unit, and it is the one that keeps a game like this closer than the ratings say.

spreads.game: Tulane Green Wave @ Army Black Knights
facts: 5.4 pts, 6.2 after the slate's own level
Army -12.1, which is 9.1 past the market
4th Success Rate, 92.9 offensive grade, 87.7 run block
135th Success Rate, 132nd Finishing Drives, 54.6 pass block
paras: Book has Army -3.0 at home. The rating says -8.4 and the points check, which knows only what each side has scored and allowed, says -12.1. The second measure is the more emphatic of the two here, which is unusual.

Army's offense is the case. It ranks 4th nationally in Success Rate on a 92.9 offensive grade, 89.9 passing and 87.7 run blocking, and they score 33.3 a game. Against a Tulane defense ranked 66th with a 56.6 coverage grade and a 51.8 tackling grade, that is a unit mismatch the three points does not price.

Tulane cannot move the ball. They rank 135th in Success Rate and 132nd in Finishing Drives behind a 54.6 pass block grade and score 18.8 a game. Their one distinction is ranking 1st in Explosiveness, which is the warning attached to this: a team that cannot sustain anything but can hit a long one is exactly the profile that steals a backdoor cover.

Army's defense is the reason this is only three: 117th in Success Rate and 121st in Havoc on a 61.5 coverage grade. Tulane at 1-3 against the spread is running behind its rating rather than ahead of it, which is the shape this card wants to be on the right side of.

facts: 5.7 pts, 4.9 after the slate's own level

51st Success Rate, 13th Finishing Drives, 89.0 run defense, 81.7 tackling
paras: Book has Oklahoma State -10.5. The rating says -4.8 and the points check says -4.0. Two measures put the fair number at under a touchdown and the market is asking for a touchdown and a half more.

The two teams are closer than the price suggests. SP+ separates them by two points, 42nd against 49th. UCF concede 17.6 a game behind a defense ranked 51st in Success Rate and 13th in Finishing Drives, on an 89.0 run defense grade and 81.7 tackling, which is the best defensive unit in the game.

Oklahoma State are the better offense, 26th in Success Rate on an 82.3 grade, and that is the honest case for laying the points. What undercuts it is 124th in Explosiveness: they move the ball steadily and do not break games open, which is the profile that struggles to cover double digits.

UCF's own offense is the problem, 102nd in Success Rate on a 55.1 passing grade, and a team that cannot score can lose by three touchdowns as easily as by seven points. Taking the points rather than the side is how the position survives that. UCF are 4-1 against the spread, so the market has been underrating them rather than the reverse.

totals.game: Coastal Carolina Chanticleers @ Marshall Thundering Herd
facts: 53.5, which is 8.7 below the market once the slate's own level is out

paras: Book has 59.0. Each team's own scoring puts the game at 53.5 and the rating at 50.9, and both sit eight to ten points below the market once the slate's level is removed. This is the widest agreement on the totals board.

Neither offense justifies a 59. Coastal Carolina score 24.8 a game on an offense ranked 99th in Success Rate and 91st in Finishing Drives; Marshall score 22.2 on one ranked 75th and 127th. Between them that is 47 points of recent form against a number asking for 59.

Marshall's defense is what built the number and it is genuinely bad: 133rd in Success Rate, 126th in Finishing Drives and 132nd in Havoc on a 49.9 coverage grade and a 50.1 tackling grade. They concede 35.0 a game. The question is whether Coastal Carolina can exploit it, and a 99th-ranked offense on a 51.2 run block grade is not the unit to assume will.

The way this loses is Marshall's defense doing what it has done all season while Coastal Carolina find 35 of their own. Both teams are 3-2 to the Over, so the records give no help in either direction.

The case against is the obvious one: this is the biggest game of the weekend between two elite defenses, Georgia grading 93.9 and Alabama 91.0, and marquee matchups tighten up. Alabama's 66.8 tackling grade and 116th rank in Explosiveness allowed is the crack in that argument.

paras: Riley has 690 rushing yards in five games, 138.0 a game, against a line of 82.5. The projection of 145.9 carries a 1.354 pace multiplier and should be read down, but it is not what this rests on: 82.5 asks for 3.8 yards a carry on his 21.6 attempts and he is at 6.4.

The volume is the foundation. 51.9% of everything Boise State run, 21.6 carries a game, and 447 of his 690 yards after contact with 24 avoided tackles on an 80.4 run grade. A back carrying that load clears a line set at 60% of his average by accumulation alone.

A 40.9% breakaway share and a long of 83 mean the distribution is lumpy, and that is the risk the card just paid for with Jadan Baugh, who went for 13 on 12 carries off a similar profile. The difference is the line: Baugh needed 5.6 a carry, Riley needs 3.8.
Boise State are 6.5-point favourites with a 27.5 implied total, which is the script that keeps a lead back on the field. Fresno State are the matchup and they are not a wall.

facts: 6.8 targets a game, 27 on the season, 108 routes

A 16.8 average depth of target is the highest on this prop card, and he converts it: 2.44 yards per route run on 108 routes, 17 catches on 27 targets, four touchdowns, a long of 37 and a 76.2 route grade. 6.8 targets a game is a real share rather than an occasional shot.
Utah carry a 33.2 implied total, the highest of any team on this card, so the offense is expected to be productive. Kansas are the matchup.

The script is the risk and it is the familiar one. Utah are 15.5-point favourites, and a favourite that large can be up three scores by the fourth quarter with its deep threat on the sideline. A 16.8 aDOT receiver in a blowout is the single most likely way this number goes unreached.

props.pick: Rodney Fields Jr. Over 53.5 Rushing Yards
facts: 12.3 carries a game, 49 on the season: 32.5% of Kansas State's carries
5.6 yards a carry against a line asking 4.3
51.5% breakaway share, only 5 avoided tackles on 49 carries
paras: Fields has 274 rushing yards in four games, 68.5 a game, against a line of 53.5. At 12.3 carries a game the line asks for 4.3 a carry and he is at 5.6.
Kansas State are near a pick'em at -2.5 with a 28.8 implied total, so there is no blowout script in either direction to take the ball out of his hands.

This is the weakest of the five and the write-up should say why rather than bury it. A 32.5% carry share is the smallest on this card, five avoided tackles and 122 yards after contact on 49 carries is thin, and a 51.5% breakaway share with a long of 75 means more than half his season came on a handful of plays. Strip the long run and he is at roughly 50 a game against a 53.5 line.

It clears the screens because the model edge, the production gap and the role floor all pass, and it is here on that basis rather than on conviction. If the card were four props instead of five, this is the one that would come off.
